title: Nigel Farage claims Sunderland have invited him to visit the Stadium of Light
content:
Nigel Farage has said he has been invited by Sunderland to visit the Stadium of Light.

The Reform UK leader, and long-time ally of U.S. president Donald Trump, has been in the city this week to launch his party’s local election campaign. He told UK broadcaster ITV that the club would like him to visit for a home game.

“I’ve been talking to one of the directors and they’d very much like to see me there,” he said, per ITV. “If I can make it I will. Clubs should want to talk to me.”

The Athletic has approached Sunderland for comment.

The Premier League side’s constituency has been held by Labour’s Lewis Atkinson since 2024, when he won the seat with a majority of 6,073. In that election, Reform’s candidate received the second-most number of votes, with a 27 per cent share.

Reform currently don’t hold a seat on the city Council, however, for which elections will be held in May.

Sunderland’s co-owner and non-executive board member Juan Sartori has a background in right-wing politics. The 45-year-old ran to lead Uruguay’s National Party in 2019, finishing second behind eventual president Luis Lacalle Pou. Sartori’s consolation prize was a role as the country’s youngest serving senator.

Farage’s announcement comes after his visit to Ipswich Town’s Portman Road ground on Monday sparked significant backlash.

He posed for photos and posted a video of himself wishing the club luck in their bid to be promoted to the Premier League.

On Tuesday morning, Ipswich told The Athletic that the politician had not been formally invited to the stadium. The Athletic, however, revealed that the invitation was extended by an associate of chief executive officer Mark Ashton and six ‘Farage 10’ Ipswich shirts were made free of charge.

Ipswich later put out a statement saying the club is “apolitical” and “does not support or endorse any individual or party”.

Reform UK is a right-wing populist party that was founded in 2018. It was originally called ‘The Brexit Party’ owing to its campaigning on a ‘clean-break’ departure from the European Union.

It has a hardline stance on illegal immigration, promoting a “clear and uncompromising plan to remove all illegal immigrants from the UK” on its website.

Reform has also pledged to scrap the UK’s net-zero target on greenhouse gas emissions if they were elected as the next government, and would opt to “leave the European Convention on Human Rights and repeal the Human Rights Act”.
